definitions.explanation: Suffix attached to a noun to mean the raw material, lumber, or substance used for something. Common in construction, cooking, and manufacturing vocabulary.
By extension, a person regarded as a useful asset or human resource, as in {人|じん}{材|ざい} (human resources) and {逸|いつ}{材|ざい} (an outstanding talent).

examples.japanese: この{家|いえ}は{杉|すぎ}{材|ざい}で{建|た}てられている。
examples.english: This house is built with cedar lumber.

examples.japanese: {建築|けんちく}{材|ざい}の{価格|かかく}が{上|あ}がっている。
examples.english: The price of building materials is rising.

examples.japanese: {新鮮|しんせん}な{食|しょく}{材|ざい}を{使|つか}って{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}る。
{当社|とうしゃ}は{人|じん}{材|ざい}を{大切|たいせつ}にしている。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{業界|ぎょうかい}でも{逸|いつ}{材|ざい}と{呼|よ}ばれている。
examples.english: She is called an exceptional talent even within the industry.

examples.japanese: グローバルに{活躍|かつやく}できる{人|じん}{材|ざい}の{育成|いくせい}が{急務|きゅうむ}だ。
examples.english: Developing talent who can thrive globally is an urgent need.

notes:
Suffix derived from {材} (material). Sense 1 (physical material) is concrete and applies to construction, cooking, and manufacturing. Sense 2 (talent) treats people as a resource and is standard in business and HR contexts.

COMPOUNDS:
- {建築|けんちく}{材|ざい}: building material
- {食|しょく}{材|ざい}: food ingredient
- {木|もく}{材|ざい}: timber; lumber
- {素|そ}{材|ざい}: raw material; subject matter
- {教|きょう}{材|ざい}: teaching material
- {人|じん}{材|ざい}: human resources; talent
- {逸|いつ}{材|ざい}: an outstanding talent
- {取|しゅ}{材|ざい}: news gathering (literally 'taking material')

SIMILAR WORDS:
- 〜{料|りょう}: ingredient; raw material — {原|げん}{料|りょう} raw materials; closer to chemistry/manufacturing
- {材料|ざいりょう}: material; ingredient — stand-alone noun, more general
